sources_considered.why: Provides the GPT-judge discrimination results and discloses that all benchmark questions were included in training.
Read to verify that the discrimination result already appeared in the September 2021 version; the fuller revised paper is cited.
Contemporaneous disclosure confirms that language models continued to produce false outputs.
The July 2022 publication does not establish that its evaluated capability held before this post.

evidence_items.publisher: Association for Computational Linguistics; Stephanie Lin, Jacob Hilton and Owain Evans; ar5iv mirror
evidence_items.locator: Section 4.4, Automated metrics vs human evaluation
evidence_items.explanation: GPT-judge classified the factual truth of answers and transferred across held-out answer-producing model families. This contradicts absolute behavioral incapacity, but all benchmark questions were represented in training, so it does not establish unrestricted factual understanding.

evidence_items.locator: Opening discussion of GPT-3, before Results
evidence_items.explanation: The developer acknowledges false outputs, consistent with the reliability concern behind Marcus's statement. Producing false answers does not establish a complete absence of truth discrimination or its proposed cause.

unresolved_gaps: GPT-judge's validation does not establish generalization to unseen factual questions.
The evidence does not isolate reference or cognitive models as the cause of truthfulness failures.
The stronger philosophical meaning of grasp is not settled by benchmark performance.
